Q: What is a hard disk drive?
Option1: Solid-state memory with no moving parts
Option2: Spinning magnetic platters with an actuator arm and heads
Option3: Optical media read by a laser

Q: Which rotational speed offers the lowest average latency among common desktop drives?
Option2: 7,200 revolutions per minute

Q: Which rotational speed is most common in thin laptops to save power and reduce noise?
Option2: 7,200 revolutions per minute

Q: Which hard drive form factor is typical for desktops and servers needing large capacity?
Option2: 3.5 inch

Q: Which hard drive form factor is typical inside laptops and small form factor PCs?
Option2: 3.5 inch

Q: What is a solid-state drive?
Option1: A drive using flash memory with no moving parts for low latency and high shock resistance
Option2: A drive using spinning platters

Q: What is Non-Volatile Memory Express (NVMe)?
Option1: A file system for flash cards
Option2: A command set and protocol optimized for PCI Express access to solid-state storage

Q: What is Serial ATA (SATA) in the context of storage?
Option2: A serial host interface for drives such as hard disks and solid-state drives

Q: What is Peripheral Component Interconnect Express (PCIe) in storage?
Option2: A high-speed serial bus used by NVMe solid-state drives and add-in cards

Q: What is the M.2 form factor?
Option1: A 2.5 inch drive bay form factor
Option2: A small card form factor that can carry either NVMe over PCIe or SATA depending on the device and motherboard slot

Q: What is mSATA?
Option1: A miniature SATA drive form factor that uses SATA signaling over a mini-PCIe style card
Option2: A memory card for cameras

Q: Which pairing provides the highest throughput and lowest latency for a single client workstation?
Option2: M.2 SATA solid-state drive
Option3: M.2 NVMe solid-state drive over PCI Express
Option4: 7,200 revolutions per minute hard disk drive

Q: Which statement about M.2 is accurate?
Option1: All M.2 drives are NVMe only
Option2: M.2 can be either NVMe over PCI Express or SATA; the motherboard slot must support the drive type
Option4: M.2 is only for Wi-Fi cards

Q: What is Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) 0?
Option2: Striping for performance with no redundancy
Option3: Striping with parity across three or more disks

Q: What is Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) 1?
Option2: Mirroring that duplicates data to another disk for redundancy

Q: What is Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) 5?
Option1: Striping with distributed parity that tolerates a single-disk failure (minimum three disks)
Option2: Mirroring only

Q: What is Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) 10?
Option2: Mirroring and striping combined (striped set of mirrored pairs; minimum four disks)

Q: Which removable storage is best for quickly transferring files between PCs without a network?
Option1: Flash drive on Universal Serial Bus
Option2: Memory card (Secure Digital) in a camera

Q: Which removable storage is most common inside digital cameras?
Option2: Secure Digital memory card

Q: Which removable storage is most suitable for distributing read-only media or archival write-once content?
Option2: Optical disc such as DVD or Blu-ray

Q: A budget desktop needs bulk storage for large media libraries with acceptable performance. Best choice?
Option2: 3.5 inch 7,200 revolutions per minute hard disk drive
Option3: 2.5 inch 5,400 revolutions per minute hard disk drive

Q: A thin laptop needs better battery life and faster boot without changing bays. Best choice?
Option2: 3.5 inch hard disk drive

Q: A video-editing workstation needs a fast scratch disk on a single drive. Best choice?
Option2: 2.5 inch SATA solid-state drive
Option3: 7,200 revolutions per minute hard disk drive

Q: Four 2 terabyte drives are configured as Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) 5. Approximate usable capacity?
Option2: 4 terabytes

Q: Four 2 terabyte drives are configured as Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) 10. Approximate usable capacity?
Option2: 4 terabytes

Q: Which statement compares 2.5 inch and 3.5 inch drives correctly?
Option1: 2.5 inch typically fits laptops; 3.5 inch typically fits desktops/servers and offers larger capacity per drive
Option2: 2.5 inch always faster than 3.5 inch
Option3: 3.5 inch uses less power than 2.5 inch in laptops

Q: Which statement compares SATA solid-state drives and hard disk drives?
Option1: SATA solid-state drives have lower latency and are shock-resistant; hard disk drives offer higher capacities per dollar
Option2: Hard disk drives are always faster

Q: What differentiates mSATA and M.2 for SSDs?
Option2: mSATA uses SATA signaling only; M.2 can be SATA or NVMe over PCI Express depending on the drive and slot
Option3: Both are only for Wi-Fi cards

Q: Why might an M.2 NVMe drive not be recognized in a particular slot?
Option2: The motherboard slot must support NVMe/PCIe and the physical keying of the drive
Option4: It requires a SATA power cable

Q: Which removable media is best for write-once distribution or archival compliance?
Option2: Optical disc such as DVD-R or BD-R (write-once)
